prompt:
Draft a procedure for continual improvement at an aerospace component manufacturer. Include data sources for improvement opportunities (audits, NCs, customer feedback, process data, benchmarking), prioritization methodology, project selection, resource allocation, implementation tracking, and effectiveness measurement. Align with ISO 9001 clause 10.3.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
ANSWER: {
    "document": "Procedure: Continual Improvement
Document Number: CI-PRO-001
Revision: 1.0
Effective Date: [Date]

1.0 Purpose
To establish a systematic process for identifying, evaluating, prioritizing, and implementing improvement opportunities to enhance the quality management system, product quality, customer satisfaction, and operational performance, in alignment with ISO 9001:2015 clause 10.3.

2.0 Scope
This procedure applies to all processes, products, and activities within the aerospace component manufacturing organization.

3.0 Responsibilities
3.1 Top Management: Ensures resources are available and promotes continual improvement.
3.2 Quality Assurance Manager: Oversees the continual improvement process, maintains records, and reports to management review.
3.3 Process Owners: Identify improvement opportunities within their areas and lead/participate in improvement projects.
3.4 All Employees: Are responsible for reporting potential improvements.

4.0 Procedure
4.1 Identification of Improvement Opportunities
Improvement opportunities shall be identified from the following data sources:
- Internal & External Audit Findings (including customer and regulatory audits)
- Nonconformities (NCs) and Corrective Actions
- Customer Feedback (including complaints, surveys, and direct communication)
- Process Performance Data (e.g., SPC, yield, scrap, rework, cycle time, delivery performance)
- Management Review Outputs
- Benchmarking against industry leaders and competitors
- Suggestions from Employees
- Analysis of Trends (e.g., in quality objectives, customer satisfaction)

4.2 Prioritization Methodology
Opportunities shall be evaluated and prioritized using a Risk-Based Approach scoring against the following criteria (scale 1-5):
- Impact on Product Safety & Airworthiness
- Impact on Customer Satisfaction
- Financial Impact (Cost of Poor Quality vs. Implementation Cost)
- Alignment with Strategic Objectives
- Feasibility and Resource Requirement
- Regulatory/Compliance Urgency
A weighted score will be calculated. Opportunities scoring above a defined threshold shall be considered for action.

4.3 Project Selection
A Continual Improvement Board (CIB), chaired by the Quality Manager with cross-functional membership, shall review prioritized opportunities quarterly. The CIB shall select projects based on the prioritization score, strategic alignment, and available resources. Selected projects shall be formally initiated with a Project Charter.

4.4 Resource Allocation
Top Management, upon recommendation from the CIB, shall allocate necessary resources (personnel, budget, equipment, time). Resource allocation shall be documented in the project charter and reviewed during management review.

4.5 Implementation Tracking
Each improvement project shall have an assigned leader responsible for developing an action plan with milestones, deadlines, and responsibilities. Progress shall be tracked using a central register and reviewed in monthly CIB meetings. Significant deviations from the plan shall trigger a review and corrective action.

4.6 Effectiveness Measurement
The effectiveness of implemented improvements shall be measured by comparing post-implementation data against baseline metrics. Key measures may include:
- Reduction in specific defect rates or NCs
- Improvement in process capability indices (Cp/Cpk)
- Increased customer satisfaction scores
- Achievement of financial targets (e.g., cost reduction)
- Verification of objective achievement
Effectiveness reviews shall be conducted 3-6 months after implementation closure. If results are unsatisfactory, the project shall be re-evaluated.

4.7 Documentation and Management Review
All improvement projects, from identification to effectiveness review, shall be recorded. A summary of continual improvement activities, their status, and results shall be an input to the Management Review meeting to ensure alignment with the strategic direction and to secure ongoing support.

5.0 Related Documents
- Corrective Action Procedure
- Management Review Procedure
- Risk Management Procedure
- Document and Record Control Procedure

6.0 Records
- Continual Improvement Opportunity Register
- Project Charters and Action Plans
- CIB Meeting Minutes
- Effectiveness Review Reports",
    "sections": "Purpose, Scope, Responsibilities, Procedure (Identification of Improvement Opportunities, Prioritization Methodology, Project Selection, Resource Allocation, Implementation Tracking, Effectiveness Measurement, Documentation and Management Review), Related Documents, Records",
    "clauseRefs": "ISO 9001:2015 Clause 10.3 (Continual Improvement)"
}
